lines.text: Snoopy worked for NASA for free.
In 1967, NASA wanted a mascot for its flight safety program.
lines.say: In nineteen sixty seven, NASA wanted a mascot for its flight safety program.

lines.text: Charles Schulz let it use Snoopy the Astronaut at no cost.
Schulz drew the picture that the award pin copies.
The pin is sterling silver and shows Snoopy in a spacesuit.
By NASA's rule, each pin flies on a mission first.
An astronaut presents it, and nobody can win it twice.
In March 1969, Schulz's strips landed Snoopy's doghouse on the Moon.
lines.say: In March nineteen sixty nine, Schulz's strips landed Snoopy's doghouse on the Moon.

lines.text: In May 1969, Apollo 10's lunar module was named Snoopy.
lines.say: In May nineteen sixty nine, Apollo ten's lunar module was named Snoopy.

lines.text: Its command module was named Charlie Brown.

post.caption: Snoopy worked for NASA for free. In 1967, NASA wanted a mascot for its flight safety program. Charles Schulz let it use Snoopy the Astronaut at no cost. Schulz drew the picture that the award pin copies. The pin is sterling silver and shows Snoopy in a spacesuit. By NASA's rule, each pin flies on a mission first. An astronaut presents it, and nobody can win it twice. In March 1969, Schulz's strips landed Snoopy's doghouse on the Moon. In May 1969, Apollo 10's lunar module was named Snoopy. Its command module was named Charlie Brown.
